leaders.priorTitle: History professor, academic dean, and senior vice president
leaders.notes: Led the institution's growth into Shenandoah University with six schools over a 26-year tenure. Retired in 2008 and was later honored as president emeritus; died October 2025 at age 80.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President (previously Dean, College of Arts & Sciences, then VP for Academic Affairs)
leaders.notes: Joined Shenandoah in 2001 as a dean and rose internally before becoming the university's 16th (and first female) president on July 1, 2008. As of 2026 she is the longest-serving sitting president among Virginia colleges and universities.

statusNote: Known as Simmons College until it adopted the Simmons University name in 2018; leadership record below uses one continuous institutional identity.

leaders.notes: Asked to serve as acting president in 1995 while leading American Student Assistance Corporation; previously president of Wheelock College (1983-1991). Appointed permanent sixth president in 1996.
Served as Simmons' sixth (permanent) president 1996-2006 after a year as acting president. Held president emeritus status afterward and remained active on nonprofit boards; died in 2011.
Seventh president of Simmons College; stepped down after two years to pursue international public health work and lead The Sage Colleges.

Eighth president; credited with stabilizing Simmons' finances over a 12-year tenure. After leaving in 2020, served as interim president of Cabrini University (overseeing its asset sale to Villanova) and later advised Northland College's board during its closure.

leaders.priorTitle: David J. Nolan Dean, Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management
leaders.notes: Ninth president and first Black president of Simmons University, effective July 1, 2020. Previously spent nearly 20 years on the faculty of the University of Michigan's Ross School of Business before her Cornell deanship.

statusNote: Knoxville is the flagship campus of a multi-campus institution (additional locations include Asheville, Indianapolis, Dallas, and others), each led locally by a 'campus president' who reports up to the Knoxville-based Chancellor. No institution-wide leadership change has occurred since Stephen A. South's 1989 acquisition; no other names for the top (Chancellor/President) post from 1996-present were found in public sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Unknown (acquired the institution, then known as Knoxville Business College)
leaders.notes: Acquired the college (then Knoxville Business College, founded 1882) in 1989, renamed it South College in 2001, and has led it continuously since, expanding it from roughly 1,000 students (2009) to more than 20,000 across multiple campuses (2025). No leadership turnover in the 1996-present window.

statusNote: South University-Columbia is a branch campus location of South University, a single multi-campus, for-profit institution headquartered in Savannah, GA (11+ ground campuses plus online). It is not separately chartered or independently accredited, and has no institution-level president/chancellor of its own -- day-to-day leadership is a Campus Director / Dean of Academic Affairs and Operations reporting to South University's system-wide CEO/Chancellor. South University separated from the nonprofit Education Principle Foundation in 2023 to return to independent for-profit status, and its current system-wide CEO and Chancellor is Benjamin J. DeGweck (effective October 31, 2025). No reliable public record of the Columbia campus's director/leadership succession back to 1996 was found, so no campus-level leaders are listed; a system-wide South University president/CEO succession record would need to be researched separately if that is the entity of interest.
